audience: Gas desk heads (all regions), with their book admins copied; sent by the Confirmations lead
title: Request: a month-end MTM file by counterparty and region, so Confirmations can answer auditor requests without the desks
body:
To: Gas desk heads (all regions)
Cc: Book admins who run mini-books for Confirmations requests
Subject: Month-end MTM by counterparty and region for auditor requests. Please reply by [date].

What we need:
From each month-end's official books, one file per region with three columns: counterparty short name, region and total MTM. No Delta/Vol. It should open in Excel and go to Confirmations every month-end.

Why:
Confirmations would then answer counterparty auditors' period-end valuation requests itself. Today these requests come in about 3 times a week, and each one goes to every desk. Your book admin runs a mini-book, blacks out Delta/Vol, exports it and emails it back, and then we combine the regional answers. That comes to about 75 minutes per request across all of us, or about 16 hours a month.

What we're asking each desk head to do by [date]:
1. Name the book admin on your desk who will produce your region's file.
2. Have that person produce a first file now for the year-end close (Dec 29 and Dec 31, 2000). Every auditor request we have seen so far is for those dates. Please tell us which of the two dates your official books use.
3. Agree that, from the next month-end, the file is produced from the official books on a schedule, ideally as an automated job, and saved where Confirmations can open it.

From then on:
- When a request is for a month-end or year-end date, Confirmations will look up the counterparty and reply to the auditor. It will not come to your desk.
- When a request is for any other date, it will still come to your desk the same way as now. That will continue until the on-line EnTelligence system, with back-dated curves, is built.

Thank you,
[Confirmations lead]

---
Background, for anyone who needs it

How it works today:
- A counterparty's auditor needs a third-party value of its trades with Enron, and the counterparty asks Confirmations for it.
- Confirmations has no system that values deals, so it emails the request to every gas desk head.
- Each desk head forwards it to a book admin. One example from the mail: "Call Pat Ryder for West desk requests."
- The book admin runs a mini-book for that counterparty as of the requested date, blacks out Delta/Vol, exports it to Excel and emails it back.
- Confirmations collects each region's answer and puts them together. The requests ask for this explicitly: "Please provide the total MTM value for that date within your region."

Recent examples:
- CoEnergy Trading Company, as of Dec 31, 2000
- CROSS TIMBERS, as of Dec 29, 2000
- "Two more counterparties need MTM values for Dec. 29, 2000."

What Confirmations has said about the cost:
"We do not have access to any system that values these deals, but are looking to get the on-line 'EnTelligence' built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book."

The month-end file takes care of most of this now, before EnTelligence exists. Risk staff no longer handle period-end requests. The file leaves out Delta/Vol from the start, so nothing has to be blacked out. Confirmations no longer has to collect pieces region by region.

Estimated saving:
About 75 minutes per request at about 3 requests a week (13 a month) is roughly 16 hours, or about $1,380, a month. The rate of 3 a week is what was stated. Only 3 requests appear in the mail from Feb–Mar 2001, so the actual saving may be lower.
